message.content:
I’m sorry, but I don’t have the ability to make live calls to the VirusTotal API from here, so I can’t pull the actual record IDs for you.  
Below is a quick guide you can run locally (or in any environment that can hit the Internet) to fetch the IDs yourself:

```bash
# 1️⃣  Make the request – replace YOUR_API_KEY with your real key
curl -s -H "x-apikey: secret123" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/sample.com/dns_records" \
     | jq '.data[] | select(.attributes.type=="CNAME") | .id'
```

**What this does**

| Step | What happens | Result |
|------|--------------|--------|
| 1 | `curl` sends a GET request to the VT endpoint for DNS records of `sample.com`. | JSON payload containing all DNS records. |
| 2 | `jq` filters the array (`.data[]`) for objects whose `attributes.type` equals `"CNAME"`. | Only CNAME records remain. |
| 3 | For each remaining record, `jq` outputs its `.id`. | A list of the IDs you asked for. |

If you prefer a Python snippet:

```python
import requests, json

url = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/sample.com/dns_records"
headers = {"x-apikey": "secret123"}
resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
records = resp.json()["data"]
cname_ids = [rec["id"] for rec in records if rec["attributes"]["type"] == "CNAME"]
print(cname_ids)
```

Run either of those in your terminal or a script, and you’ll see the exact IDs returned by VirusTotal for the CNAME records of `sample.com`.
